content.title: About
content.content: Meat loaf made with ham is a baked dish prepared from ground meat (usually beef or pork), finely diced ham, eggs, breadcrumbs and seasonings. It has a dense texture, a fragrant ham flavor and a tender taste, suitable as a main course or a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The tradition of making meat loaf dates back to medieval Europe, where it was known as "pot-loaf".
Ham in the recipe adds not only flavor but also extra moisture to the finished loaf.
Meat loaf is often served with gravy or tomato sauce.
In some regions it is glazed with ketchup or barbecue sauce for a sweet‑savory finish.
The dish slices easily into portions, making it popular for picnics and school lunches.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The ground meat and ham provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Red meat contains heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Ham and meat are abundant in vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc contributes to immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Moderate healthy fats
items.content: When balanced with lean meat, the loaf can provide beneficial monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Large amounts of meat and ham can raise saturated fat levels, which may be undesirable for heart‑related conditions.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Ham often contains added salt and nitrites; people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Undercooked ground meat may harbor pathogens; ensure the loaf reaches an internal temperature of 71 °C.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have an allergy or intolerance to certain types of meat.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the meat loaf into thick or thin pieces and serve hot or cold. It pairs well with mustard, gravy, tomato sauce, or simply as a sandwich filling. Complement with mashed potatoes, vegetable sides and fresh salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the cooked loaf to room temperature, then wrap tightly in plastic film or place in an airtight container. Store in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. For longer keeping, freeze in portion‑sized slices – up to 3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 74 °C before serving.
